metaData.originalTitle: Holo3.1: Fast & Local Computer Use Agents
metaData.title: Holo3.1: Fast & Local Computer Use Agents
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Holo3.1 is a new family of computer-use AI models that improves robustness across web, desktop, and mobile environments, introduces quantized checkpoints for local inference, and offers multiple sizes for cost-performance tradeoffs.
metaData.summary: This article announces the release of the Holo3.1 family of computer-use agents, building on the previous Holo3 model. The key improvements are threefold: enhanced robustness across diverse environments (web, desktop, and mobile), better integration with various agent frameworks via native function-calling support, and the introduction of quantized checkpoints (FP8, Q4 GGUF, NVFP4) for local and on-device inference. The model family includes four sizes (0.8B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B) to cater to different deployment needs, from ultra-lightweight local agents to state-of-the-art performance. The article provides benchmark results showing significant gains on mobile automation (AndroidWorld) and cross-harness performance, and details the speedups achieved with quantization, particularly on NVIDIA's DGX Spark hardware. The release is positioned as a major step toward universal, private, and locally executable computer-use agents.

mainPoints.point: Holo3.1 improves robustness across web, desktop, and mobile environments.
mainPoints.explanation: The model family is designed to handle distribution shifts encountered in production, with significant gains on mobile benchmarks like AndroidWorld (from 67% to 79.3% for the 35B model).

mainPoints.point: Native function-calling support enables seamless integration with third-party agent frameworks.
mainPoints.explanation: In addition to structured JSON outputs, Holo3.1 supports function-calling protocols, achieving near-parity performance with native execution across various benchmarks.

mainPoints.point: Quantized checkpoints (FP8, Q4 GGUF, NVFP4) enable fast, local, and private inference.
mainPoints.explanation: For the first time, the Holo family offers quantized weights. NVFP4 on DGX Spark delivers a 1.74x throughput increase over BF16 with minimal performance loss, enabling fully local agent execution.

mainPoints.point: The model family offers multiple sizes for cost-performance tradeoffs.
mainPoints.explanation: Sizes range from 0.8B for ultra-lightweight local agents to 35B-A3B for state-of-the-art performance, allowing developers to choose the right balance for their deployment scenario.

keyQuotes: Holo3.1 is a major step toward our vision of universal computer-use agents: systems that can operate across environments, integrate into any agent stack, and run wherever the workflow lives.
As teams moved Holo3 from evaluation to production, we repeatedly observed the same challenge: strong performance in one setting does not necessarily transfer to another.

The agent itself runs locally on a Windows or Mac machine, while the model can either run on that same machine...or on a DGX Spark on the same network. In both cases, execution stays fully private and local, with nothing leaving the user's network.
